title: Testing raw shell completion output via env vars in CliRunner

note.title: Testing raw shell completion output via env vars in CliRunner
answers: how to test zsh completion output in click
simulate tab completion in a click test
note.body:
In tests/test_shell_completion.py, call `runner.invoke(cli, env={...})` with `_<PROG>_COMPLETE` set to `<shell>_complete` (e.g. `_CLI_COMPLETE=zsh_complete` for a group named `cli`). Pass `COMP_WORDS` (the words typed so far, e.g. "a c:") and `COMP_CWORD` (the index of the word being completed).
Apply `@pytest.mark.usefixtures("_patch_for_completion")` so the invocation goes through the completion path.
Then assert on `result.output`. For zsh each item is three lines (type, value, help, with `_` meaning no help), so `textwrap.dedent` triple-quoted strings make the expected output easy to read. See test_zsh_full_complete_with_colons.
